title: Platform Resource Identity and Brand Governance shadow and governed-foundation contract

phases.objective: Define and test deterministic identity, Brand resolution, claim verification, and operation governance contracts while keeping relationship, authority, grant, credential, migration apply, and Production mutation separate.

e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: The resolver returns an identity-safe EXACT/PROBABLE/NONE/CONFLICT/AMBIGUOUS decision without exposing candidate tenant ownership or creating authority.
steps: Normalize the submitted identifiers using the registered identifier type.
Filter candidate rows to the requested tenant scope before resolution output.
Apply hard identifier, probable identifier, and ambiguity rules deterministically.
Return only brand_id, matched identifier types, evidence readiness, reasons, and disclosure policy.
Require separate authority resolution for any future relationship or mutation operation.
assertions: A unique fresh verified hard identifier resolves EXACT.
Name-only matching resolves PROBABLE or AMBIGUOUS and never EXACT.
Multiple hard matches resolve CONFLICT and do not merge.
No candidate tenant_id appears in resolver output.
Relationship validation never creates a grant and always sets authority_implied=false.
No database connection, migration apply, credential read, provider call, external send, or Production mutation occurs in this slice.

e2e_journeys.actor: Governed verification worker with explicit expected revision
e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: Verification evidence is recorded and a claim relationship is updated only with expected-revision control; no authority grant is created.
steps: Create a deterministic challenge reference without including secrets.
Record evidence using a hash and safe metadata filtering.
Verify the claim only when current evidence is verified and expected_revision matches.
Activate only the tenant-to-Brand relationship represented by the claim.
Return authority_grant_mutated=false and fail closed on stale revisions.
assertions: Secret-like metadata keys are excluded from persisted metadata.
A stale expected revision returns a conflict and does not update the claim.
Relationship verification does not imply or create an authority grant.
The mocked regression path performs no database connection, migration apply, provider call, credential read, or Production mutation.

e2e_journeys.actor: Tenant-scoped signed principal with workspace-owner evidence
e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: The claim lifecycle remains an owner-gated, revision-aware library contract with explicit shadow-only authority boundaries; no route or Production authority is activated.
steps: Require the exact tenant workspace owner/admin membership before reading or mutating a claim.
Resolve one canonical Brand identity before relationship or claim verification proceeds.
Create, list, challenge, submit evidence, and revoke claims with deterministic status and expected-revision behavior.
Return safe evidence and relationship projections without credentials, grants, provider dispatch, or external sends.
assertions: Zero or multiple membership/claim rows fail closed rather than selecting an arbitrary context.
Brand claim lifecycle helpers remain library-only and do not register HTTP routes.
No authority grant, migration apply, database connection, credential read, provider call, or Production mutation occurs in the synthetic tests.

e2e_journeys.actor: Canonical resource identity reader with explicit workspace scope
e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: Workspace Brand identity is created/read through a dual-read, canonical-resource library contract while route wiring and runtime authority remain disabled.
steps: Resolve a canonical Brand reference by stable resource identity and bounded legacy alias fallback.
Require active Brand status and exact row cardinality before exposing the read model.
Preserve explicit authority-binding and grant shapes as shadow contracts without executing grants or provider mutations.
Keep global Brand creation and lifecycle projections separate from HTTP route registration and Production activation.
assertions: Canonical Brand read authority fails closed on missing, ambiguous, or inactive identity rows.
Workspace lifecycle and authority helpers do not register routes or become runtime authority in this slice.
No database connection, migration apply, grant, credential read, provider call, external send, or Production mutation occurs in the synthetic tests.

e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: Brand and platform operation governance decisions remain deterministic registry evidence; no route execution, grant, provider dispatch, or Production mutation is performed.
steps: Resolve the canonical operation registry entry and compare it with the governed operation contract.
Require explicit shadow-only execution metadata and fail closed on missing or conflicting governance.
Emit structured operation evidence without executing a route, applying a grant, reading credentials, or invoking a provider.
assertions: The canonical registry and operation governance contract tests pass.
Registry evidence does not become runtime route wiring or execution authority in Spec 020.
No database connection, migration apply, grant, credential read, provider call, external send, or Production mutation occurs in the synthetic tests.

e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: The authored SQL migration satisfies the repository MariaDB collation contract and remains unapplied.
steps: Inspect only changed migration SQL against the current MariaDB policy.
Require explicit utf8mb4 charset and utf8mb4_uca1400_ai_ci collation for all projected tables and columns.
Emit a no-apply readiness report with database_connection_performed=false and sql_mutation_performed=false.
Keep migration apply, backfill, grants, and Production promotion behind separate authority.
assertions: The migration passes the MariaDB collation guard.
No database connection or SQL apply occurs.
No credentials, provider writes, grants, or Production mutations occur.
The migration contract test passes independently of live database state.
